# 0007: Use Varlock for environment contracts

## Status

Accepted

## Decision

The template uses Varlock instead of maintaining the former Metaideas environment
package. Package workspaces own reusable contract fragments and application workspaces
own complete resolved schemas. This keeps validation close to the code that consumes a
value while making each runnable application's environment readable from one file.

A package exposes only the surfaces it needs under `env/`: shared values are
non-sensitive across runtimes, client values are explicitly bundle-safe, server values
belong to a server runtime and may be sensitive, and build values belong to build,
upload, or deployment tooling and must not enter a client bundle. Varlock 1.16 requires
imported fragments to use `.env.*` names, so the standard surfaces are named
`.env.shared`, `.env.client`, `.env.server`, and `.env.build` rather than the originally
planned `shared.env`, `client.env`, `server.env`, and `build.env` spellings.

Each workspace root `.env.schema` is the contract. Committed `.env.development` files
contain safe local values, ignored `.env.local` files may override them, and deployment
platforms own preview and production values. Generated TypeScript is local to its
workspace, committed, regenerated by `bun run codegen`, and checked for deterministic
output in CI. Global environment augmentation stays disabled so one workspace cannot
claim that another workspace's variables exist.

Sensitivity metadata and the selected framework integration are the client security
boundary; public-looking prefixes remain only where a framework or platform requires
them. Vite, Astro, WXT, Expo/Metro, and Tauri use their Varlock integration. Expo's
JavaScript application configuration retains documented `process.env` compatibility
because Expo evaluates that configuration before application modules. Bun's automatic
dotenv loading is disabled and Varlock-managed runtime commands are wrapped so only
one precedence model populates the process.

Convex is an intentional independent boundary. Backend functions declare their native
variables in `convex.config.ts`, consume Convex's generated `env` API, and parse
structured values locally. Convex deployment values and deploy keys remain in Convex;
Varlock does not synchronize secrets into it. Consuming applications declare only the
non-sensitive Convex URLs they require.

Plain deployment-platform secrets are the supported default. A scaffold owner may add
a Varlock secret-store plugin; 1Password is documented as the reference workflow, but
the template contains no vault, account, organization, or item identifiers. Secret
resolution must target development, preview, or production explicitly and occur before
a remote mutation without printing resolved values.

Plan 17 had not recorded its required pass when this decision was implemented. On
2026-08-05, the template owner explicitly waived that gate and accepted the integration
risk. Two behavior differences are also accepted: Varlock currently parses trusted
origin lists as string arrays without the former per-origin regular expression, and
credentialed Convex/EAS deployment checks remain operational checks rather than local
test evidence.

## Consequences

`@init/env`, `@tooling/env`, T3 Env, and `.env.template` are removed. Template commands
compose application schema keys idempotently, generated types keep global augmentation
disabled, environment checks reject missing required values, and the artifact scanner
rejects sensitive canaries in client outputs. Scaffold owners may replace Varlock later,
but a new scaffold receives one coherent environment system.
